messages:
Alex Kim: quick heads-up — I started a stress run on long-context chat sessions and see sustained KV cache growth that correlates with continuous-batching merge events. repro on dev-gpu-2.
Priya Singh: can you paste the minimal repro?
Alex Kim: steps: 1) run `./loadtest --model rdl/opt-16k --clients 120 --ctx 12k --pattern chat` 2) enable `CONT_BATCH=1` and `KV_PREFETCH=on` 3) watch `kv_residency` and `mem.rss`.
Alex Kim: snippet from the profiler (just after 30m):
```
# heap-profile
heap_live_bytes: 1.9GB
kv_fragment_count: 4723
avg_kv_slot_size: 4096
evict_rate_per_min: 18
contbatch_merge_events: 1.2k
```
Priya Singh: hmm — eviction rate looks high but not keeping up with allocation. Any head-of-line blocking logs?
Alex Kim: yes, `runtime` logs show repeated `batch_merge_wait` for head-slot 0, followed by large `kv_slot_pin` durations. Example: `WARN batch_merge_wait 0->1 dur=42ms kv_pin=120ms slot_cnt=18`
Ben Torres: sounds like cont-batch is merging many partial batches that pin old KV fragments longer than expected. If a merged batch includes a token sequence that references a long-tail context, the KV pager can't evict because pins cross-request boundaries.
Priya Singh: can you dump `kv_slot_owner` for a high-residency shard?
Alex Kim: attached small table (inline): `shard-3: owners=[cli-12, cli-12, cli-34, cli-12, cli-78, cli-12, ...]` — lots of repeated owners from same client which is odd; pattern: multiple simultaneous partial batches from same source getting merged.
Ben Torres: hypothesis: merge window heuristics are too permissive when batch arrival variance is high. We end up merging many partials, increasing the lifespan of some KV fragments because they are referenced by the merged mega-batch head. Also fragmentation increases because smaller slots are left behind when pinned.
Priya Singh: can we try limiting `merge_max_slots` and `merge_age_ms` and see effect?
Alex Kim: tried `merge_max_slots=8` (default 64) and `merge_age_ms=6` (default 30). Results after 25m: `heap_live_bytes` down to 1.05GB, `kv_fragment_count` 1900, `evict_rate_per_min` 40. No more HOL warnings in logs.
Ben Torres: nice. That suggests the HOL blocking was from giant merges holding onto heterogeneous KV fragments. We should instrument a metric: `contbatch.merge.kv_pin_ms` and gate an adaptive heuristic: if `kv_residency_ratio > 0.6` then reduce merge window.
Alex Kim: agree. Also saw fragmentation pattern: when a merge includes a mixture of short and long contexts, we get many small leftover fragments because we pack long and short sequences into same merged batch. Could add batch coalescing by similarity of context length.
Priya Singh: or prefer aligning merges by client affinity so we avoid cross-client pinning — e.g., merge only batches from same client or same ctx-len bucket. That reduces kv_slot churn.
Ben Torres: tradeoff: more selective merges => lower throughput but better memory stability. We should run experiments on throughput vs cost. I'll sketch an A/B: control=default merge, experiment=merge_max_slots=8 + affinity=true.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary group (dev-gpu-2) will run experiment config for 1h starting now. :rocket:
Alex Kim: quick follow-up: profiling trace shows kernel selection spikes during these merged requests — some fused attention kernels get selected for long contexts, increasing per-request memory working set. So the issue is composite: batching heuristics -> merged request shapes -> kernel choice -> kv residency.
Priya Singh: good catch. So change set likely touches batching heuristic, an affinity gate, and add a kernel selection fallback that prefers lower working-set kernels for merged requests beyond a threshold.
Ben Torres: action items: 1) Alex — collect full pprof and kv slot owner dump for 2 hours (assigned) 2) Priya — prototype `merge_max_slots` and affinity toggle + run perf A/B (assigned) 3) Ben — add metric `contbatch.merge.kv_pin_ms` and an alert if >100ms sustained (assigned).
Alex Kim: I'll drop the initial pprof into the thread after collection. thanks. :thumbsup:
Priya Singh: if the canary looks good we can roll to dedicated staging tomorrow.
Alex Kim: noted. Also adding a short repro gist: `https://gist.github.com/redwood/kv-contbatch-repro-175913`
Ben Torres: perfect. let's sync in 24h.
